boundary_rationale: This row opens the book’s third-person frame with the superscription “The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:” (web:Eccl.1.1). The verse leads with the construct דִּבְרֵי֙ קֹהֶ֣לֶת (oshb:Eccl.1.1, byte tier), the sole superscription among four verse-initial ḏivrei sites in the book — the other three sit mid-discourse as genitive phrases rather than headers (sweep: 4 verses). The royal formula בֶּן דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Eccl.1.1, byte tier) supplies the frame’s own king-identification, distinct in voice from the monologue’s later first-person self-identification.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the motto that follows was rejected because the superscription is a third-person editorial title standing outside the monologue proper, while the motto that follows is itself a further third-person utterance -- one of three amar-qohelet frame intrusions in the book (1:2, 7:27, 12:8) -- naming Qohelet by his own said-formula rather than speaking in Qohelet's own first-person monologue voice.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: This frame verse itself carries no hevel token and no tachat-hashemesh formula; both begin inside the same F1 prologue poem this verse opens, well before the monologue itself begins -- hevel first at the doubled superlative הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.2, byte tier) and tachat-hashemesh first at תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.1.3, byte tier), both ahead of the monologue's own opening at Eccl.1.12.

boundary_rationale: A self-address formula opens the mirth experiment: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.1, byte tier) — “I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.” (web:Eccl.2.1). The bare amarti token itself recurs one verse later inside this row's own span at 2:2 and so cannot by itself certify the row's opening; what marks 2:1 as a genuine restart is this formula's pairing with a freshly stated experiment (the mirth-and-pleasure test) rather than the token's mere presence, since the same self-address formula (skeleton tier) recurs verse-initially at web:Eccl.2.15, וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, skeleton tier), without opening a row there — that verse continues the fool's-fate reflection rather than naming a new experiment. The row closes on the laughter verdict of 2:2, “It is foolishness… What does it accomplish?” (web:Eccl.2.2), a short self-contained test-and-verdict unit that ends before the wine-and-works experiment of 2:3 opens with its own תַּ֣רְתִּי verb (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) — the verb that changes at that seam, not the shared be-libbi heart-idiom, which continues from 2:1 through 2:3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this row into the works catalogue that follows was rejected: 2:1-2 tests mirth and laughter specifically and reaches its own vanity verdict before 2:3 pivots to a materially different experiment (wine, building, and accumulation) under a new verb, תַּ֣רְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), even though the surrounding be-libbi heart-idiom persists across the seam.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The bare hevel token here is not the monologue's first occurrence: 1:2's occurrences belong to the frame motto outside this row, but web:Eccl.1.14 (וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, oshb:Eccl.1.14, byte tier), already carries it — disclosed here rather than implied absent.

boundary_rationale: The time catalogue is chunked as one row by its own registered function: 26 of its 29 et-slots govern an infinitive across 3:2-3:7 and 3:8's own opening pair, לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ / לִשְׂנֹ֔א ('to love' / 'to hate') (byte tier, re-tally: 26/29 infinitival); the remaining 3 govern nouns or a prepositional phrase — 3:1's own וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier, 'a time for every purpose/matter') and 3:8's own closing pair עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Eccl.3.8, byte tier, 'a time for war, and a time for peace'). The catalogue opens, לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier) — “For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:” (web:Eccl.3.1) — and closes, עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Eccl.3.8, byte tier), “a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.” (web:Eccl.3.8).
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Eccl.3.1 (setumah, single-witness, tier-3: this samekh terminates the verse -- the same seg-shape as the petuchah at oshb:Eccl.1.11 -- marking an internal division preceding the 3:2-8 series -- never a boundary driver; this row's unity rests on the catalogue's own registered function, not this mark)
oshb:Eccl.3.8 (setumah, single-witness, tier-3 bracket closing the catalogue)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the catalogue at its own antithetical pairs (birth/death, plant/uproot, and so on) was rejected under the list's own function: the fourteen paired clauses form one register unit, not fourteen independent sayings.

device_notes: The et-token distribution runs one slot at 3:1 (plus the book's sole zman) then four per verse across 3:2-3:8 (sweep: 29 tokens across the poem); of these, 26 govern an infinitive and 3 govern nouns or a prepositional phrase -- 3:1's own et (governing חֵ֖פֶץ, oshb:Eccl.3.1, 'purpose/matter') and 3:8's own closing pair עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Eccl.3.8, 'war' and 'peace'), both nouns, not the verse's opening לֶֽאֱהֹב֙/לִשְׂנֹ֔א (oshb:Eccl.3.8) infinitive pair.

boundary_rationale: The animal-comparison argument runs across these three verses as one continuous clause chain: 3:19 itself opens on a causal subordinate clause, כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי הָאָדָ֜ם (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) — “For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals…” (web:Eccl.3.19) — dependent on the animal catchword (behemah) already opened at web:Eccl.3.18, and carries וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) into the dust-return statement of 3:20, closing that same verse on כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier), one of six hakol-hevel verses book-wide. The row closes on מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ (oshb:Eccl.3.21, byte tier) — “Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?” (web:Eccl.3.21) — the same who-knows formula web:Eccl.2.19 also carries, elsewhere in this monologue, as its own closing verdict; treated consistently here, the formula again marks this row's own close, though at 3:21 it stands genuinely unanswered (no candidate answer is proposed, unlike 2:19's own wise-man-or-fool alternatives) rather than being itself the site of a fresh restart, before a distinct raiti-formula opens the next row's own verdict at 3:22.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 3:22 was rejected: 3:22 opens with its own raiti ('I saw') formula and reaches an independent nothing-better verdict, functioning as the reflection's own closing gnomic statement rather than a fourth clause of the animal-comparison argument.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: This row makes no divine-name claim; the surrounding Elohim-family count is not invoked here since no Elohim token falls within this row's own span. The row's own span also carries a hakol-hevel instance at web:Eccl.3.19 (quoted in boundary_rationale above) — one of 6 hakol-hevel verses book-wide — disclosed here as the row's own refrain content.

boundary_rationale: A fresh raiti-formula closes the ch. 3 reflection in one verse: וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ (oshb:Eccl.3.22, byte tier) — “Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion…” (web:Eccl.3.22). The verse closes on a forward-looking rhetorical question, “…for who can bring him to see what will be after him?” (web:Eccl.3.22), which this row treats as its own self-contained gnomic close rather than as the opening of the oppression observation that follows in ch. 4.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Joining this verse to the animal-comparison argument of web:Eccl.3.19-Eccl.3.21 was rejected on the strength of its own raiti restart formula and independent nothing-better verdict, distinct from the unanswered spirit-direction question that closes web:Eccl.3.21.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: This one-verse row's own closing seam (3:22|4:1) carries a shared-root catchword the bytes do disclose: this row's own closing infinitive לִרְא֔וֹת (oshb:Eccl.3.22, byte tier, 'to see') and the following row's opening verb וָאֶרְאֶה֙ (oshb:Eccl.4.1, byte tier, 'and I saw') both draw on the root ראה; it is disclosed and weighed here rather than left silent -- the row's own independent raiti-restart and nothing-better verdict still stand as this row's own boundary despite it, since 3:22's own instance sits inside a rhetorical question ('who can bring him to see...') while 4:1's is a fresh first-person perception-verb opening a materially distinct oppression observation, not a repeated clause or formula. Its opening seam (3:21|3:22) carries its own shared-root catchword: הָאָדָם֙ (oshb:Eccl.3.22, byte tier) repeats the definite noun 'the man' from web:Eccl.3.21's own הָאָדָ֔ם (oshb:Eccl.3.21, byte tier), a genuine content-token catchword straddling that boundary; it is disclosed and weighed here rather than left silent -- the row's own independent raiti-restart and nothing-better verdict still stand as this row's own boundary despite it, since the shared token is a single noun, not a repeated clause or formula. The verse's own טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר (oshb:Eccl.3.22, byte tier) is a genuine tov-min comparative construction, one of six such constructions book-wide.

boundary_rationale: A shavti turning-formula opens the row, וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ (oshb:Eccl.4.1, byte tier) — “Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun…” (web:Eccl.4.1) — one of three shavti/veshavti sites in the book (sweep: 3 verses). The oppression observation escalates through the dead-versus-living comparison of 4:2 to the row’s own closing verdict, “Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.” (web:Eccl.4.3), before a fresh raiti-verb opens the envy observation at 4:4.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 4:4 was rejected: 4:4 opens with its own raiti ('I saw') observation formula and a materially distinct topic (labor-driven envy rather than the oppressed-and-uncomforted), a clean restart point.

device_notes: A paseq seg (single-witness, count-only, no positional claim made) falls at oshb:Eccl.4.1; not engaged as a boundary driver here.

boundary_rationale: A second shavti turn opens the row, וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.4.7, byte tier) — “Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.” (web:Eccl.4.7) — the same resumptive formula (skeleton tier; the 4:1 and 4:7 openers share their consonantal skeleton but differ in cantillation, not byte-identical) that opened web:Eccl.4.1, וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י (oshb:Eccl.4.1, byte tier), here introducing the solitary toiler observation of 4:8: “There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother… This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.” (web:Eccl.4.8). MT 4:8 carries a paseq seg (single-witness, count-only) and, immediately before its own qere, an inline unpointed ketiv: גַּם עיניו עֵינ֖וֹ (oshb:Eccl.4.8) -- the plural ketiv directly preceding the singular qere, quoted here from the verse's own bytes.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row back to include 4:1-3 was rejected: 4:7 restarts the shavti formula fresh, marking a new observation cycle rather than a continuation of the earlier oppression comparison.
